name: Astrid unvalidated restaked-token withdrawal
summary: AstridProtocol.withdraw accepted any contract as the restaked token. Withdrawal processing trusted the fake token's stakedTokenAddress() and scaledBalanceToBalance(), so attacker-deployed tokens booked the protocol's real stETH, rETH and cbETH as claimable and claim() paid them out.
notes: The proxy's first implementation was equally exploitable (it checked the whitelist entry of the token the fake contract reported), but the code the system ran at the exploit was installed by the recorded upgrade, so rule 9 ages from it.
Loss is the victim basket at market price when it moved (rule 14), not the attacker's realised ETH, which differs by under 0.1%.
